issues.description: The Bitmap24 class constructor declaration in the template header declares a 3-parameter constructor (int i_width, int i_height, int depth), but the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines a 2-parameter constructor (int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses a 2-parameter constructor in its header. This mismatch between the template header and its implementation (and between template and solution) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the intended constructor signature and may lead to compilation/linking problems or ambiguous expectations when they implement or use the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template header and implementation consistent. Either change the template header to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) (matching the .cpp and the solution) or add/implement the 3-argument constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) in Bitmap24.cpp. Preferably align the template header with the solution (two-argument constructor) to avoid confusing students.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 constructor API is inconsistent between the template and solution example_program code. In the template's example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp the constructor is declared as Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) (includes an extra 'depth' parameter), whereas the template implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution's example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares the constructor with two parameters (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)). This mismatch of constructor signatures for the same conceptual entity (the Bitmap24 constructor) creates confusion for students and can produce compilation/linkage errors when comparing template and solution or when building student code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration consistent across template and solution. Recommended: update example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) (remove the third 'depth' parameter) so it matches the implementation and the solution. Alternatively, if the 'depth' parameter is required, add it to the implementation and the solution header consistently. Ensure headers and implementations match to avoid student confusion and build errors.
